The DB isn't fresh — that's the whole story. The volume `family-tree-dev_dev_pgdata` still holds an ancient pre-1.0 dev database:

```
alembic_version = v1_0_0_baseline
tables: 16 (no geocode_cache, background_jobs, backup_records, friendships, feature_flag_overrides, …)
members columns: firstName, lastName, imageData, isCollapsed, positionX, positionY
```

`positionX`/`isCollapsed` on `members` haven't existed since layout moved to dagre — this schema predates v1.0.0 by a long way.

**What happened:** the old DB was stamped with a pre-squash revision that no longer exists in the chain, so [init_db.py:70](backend/app/db/init_db.py:70) took the recovery path and ran `command.stamp(cfg, "v1_0_0_baseline", purge=True)`. That path assumes "unknown revision" means "a database that already has the full v1.0.0 schema, just labelled with a removed revision id." This one didn't — it sat at an *early* pre-squash revision. The stamp wrote a lie into `alembic_version`, and `upgrade head` then ran the post-baseline migrations against a schema that never had `geocode_cache`, blowing up at [v1_5_0_linked_tree_geocode.py:69](backend/alembic/versions/v1_5_0_linked_tree_geocode.py:69).

The v1_1_0 → v1_4_0 steps in your log "succeeded" only inside the transaction; Postgres transactional DDL rolled them all back, which is why `legal_acceptances` isn't in the table list either.

**Fix:** wipe the volume. There's nothing to lose — 0 trees, 0 members, and the only users are `admin` and `testuser`.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml down -v && docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d db
```

Then restart the backend; it'll run `v1_0_0_baseline` from scratch and walk the chain to head. Want me to run that?

One thing worth flagging separately: the purge-stamp recovery in `init_db` has no guard that the schema actually matches the baseline. A cheap check — verify a table the baseline creates but early pre-squash revisions didn't (e.g. `geocode_cache`) exists before stamping, and fail loudly with "this database predates the v1.0.0 baseline; recreate it" otherwise — would turn this silent corruption into a clear message. ```
alembic_version = v1_9_0_tree_last_opened_per_user   (full chain applied)

So the hash in the DB matches `FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in your repo-root `.env` right now, and the endpoint accepts it. Two likely explanations for what you're typing:

**1. You're using a different password than the one in `.env`.** The admin was re-seeded from scratch when the volume was wiped, so it now uses the literal value at [.env:39](.env:39) — an 8-character string that is neither `admin` nor `change-me` (the `.env.example` placeholder). The old admin in the ancient volume may well have had a different one; that hash is gone.

**2. Username case.** [auth.py:118](backend/app/api/routes/auth.py:118) matches exactly — `db.scalar(select(User).where(User.username == payload.username))`. `Admin` fails, `admin` works. Worth checking if your browser is autocapitalizing the field.

Note `_seed_admin` only runs when the user table is empty ([init_db.py:120](backend/app/db/init_db.py:120)), so editing `FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` after the first boot has no effect — but that isn't what happened here, since the current `.env` value verifies against the stored hash.

Also, if you've been retrying a lot, [auth.py:110](backend/app/api/routes/auth.py:110) rate-limits per IP+username and returns 429 with "Too many failed login attempts" — different message, but it'd block you even once you type the right thing. Restarting the backend clears the in-memory limiter.

One nit worth knowing: your dev password is 8 bytes and on the placeholder blocklist. [config.py:203](backend/app/core/config.py:203) only enforces the 12-byte non-placeholder rule in production, so dev boots fine — but that same `.env` would fail startup in a prod deployment.

name: Release

# Manual release pipeline: verify -> bump -> PR -> checks + E2E (via the
# normal PR trigger) -> merge -> publish images -> tag + GitHub Release.
#
# The release commit lands on `main` through a normal PR/squash-merge rather
# than a direct push, because the "Main" ruleset requires every change to go
# through a PR and has no bypass actors configured. required_approving_review
# _count is 0 and no CODEOWNERS file exists, so the PR merges automatically
# once its checks (the existing check-build.yml + e2e.yml, triggered exactly
# as they are for any other PR) pass — no bypass, no extra token, no settings
# change needed.
#
# publish-images.yml is still called directly (not left to main's push
# trigger) because a push produced by GITHUB_TOKEN — which is what merging a
# PR via the API does — does not trigger other workflow runs either. See the
# epic's constraint note (#899, #902).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: "Version segment to bump"
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
        required: true
      dry_run:
        description: "Compute the version and notes only — no commit, PR, or publish"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  packages: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  bump:
    name: "Bump version & open release PR"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
      pr_number: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.pr_number }}
    steps:
      - name: "Require main"
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.ref }}" != "refs/heads/main" ]; then
            echo "Releases can only be dispatched from main (got ${{ github.ref }})."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: "Checkout main"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: main
          # Full history + tags: git-cliff needs to find the previous tag.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: "Set up Node.js"
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: "Bump version files"
        id: bump
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          node scripts/bump-version.js ${{ inputs.bump }}
          echo "version=$(jq -r .version package.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: "Generate release notes"
        id: cliff
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --unreleased --tag v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} --strip header -o RELEASE_NOTES.md

Both symptoms are the same root cause, so the `gh pr checks` failure isn't a separate bug to chase.

The runs on PR [#1000](https://github.com/maxi-smidt/family-tree/pull/1000) *were* created — they're just parked:

```
CI, E2E, CodeQL, Security Scan, PR Title Lint
  event = pull_request, triggering_actor = github-actions[bot]
  status = completed, conclusion = action_required
```

`action_required` means "queued, awaiting manual approval." A run in that state has produced no check runs against the head SHA, so `gh pr checks 1000 --watch` sees zero checks and exits 1 immediately — `--watch` doesn't wait for checks to *appear*, only for existing ones to finish.

And here's why they need approval:

```
GET /repos/maxi-smidt/family-tree/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval
→ {"approval_policy": "first_time_contributors"}
```

`github-actions[bot]` has no merged contributions to this repo, so it trips the first-time-contributor gate as the PR author.

## Automating it

Two routes, and the tradeoff matters because of how your pipeline is built.

**Flip the policy** — one call, but it applies to fork PRs from real first-time contributors too, on a public repo:

```bash
gh api -X PUT repos/maxi-smidt/family-tree/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval -f approval_policy=none
```

**Create the PR with a PAT instead** — what I'd recommend. A fine-grained PAT on your own account (Contents: read/write, Pull requests: read/write) stored as a secret, used *only* for the `gh pr create` step at [release.yml:106](.github/workflows/release.yml:106):

```yaml
- name: "Commit and open release PR"
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
```

You're the repo owner, so the PR author isn't a first-time contributor and the runs start immediately. No secrets currently exist on the repo (`gh secret list` is empty), so this would be the first.

**Important: don't extend that token to the merge step.** [release.yml:11-17](.github/workflows/release.yml:11) documents that the pipeline calls `publish-images.yml` explicitly *because* a GITHUB_TOKEN merge doesn't trigger the push workflows. Keep `gh pr merge` on `${{ github.token }}`.

A GitHub App token via `actions/create-github-app-token` is the tidier long-term shape (no expiry churn), but a freshly installed App may hit the same first-time-contributor gate on its first PR — your own PAT provably won't.

`github-release` declares `needs: [bump, land, publish]` at [release.yml:203](.github/workflows/release.yml:203), and `publish` failed — both the backend and frontend image jobs died on the same `actions/attest@v3` step. A job whose `needs` didn't succeed is skipped, so everything downstream fell over in sequence.

Two things worth knowing about that job:

**There's no separate `git tag` step.** The tag is a side effect of [release.yml:225](.github/workflows/release.yml:225):

```bash
gh release create "v${version}" --target "${sha}" ...
```

`gh release create` creates the tag when it doesn't already exist. So the missing tag and the missing Release aren't two failures — they're one skipped job.

**It couldn't have succeeded anyway.** The job's "Download SBOMs" step pulls `pattern: sbom-*` to attach as release assets, but "Upload SBOM artifact" was skipped in the publish job right after the attest failure. So even with a looser gate, `download-artifact` would have failed on an empty pattern match. Two independent blockers from the same root cause.

The gating itself is correct — you don't want a tag and a published Release pointing at images that never made it out. What the failure exposed is that the *ordering* only half-protects you: "Build and push" (step 10) succeeded before the attestation (step 13) failed, so the registry was already mutated and `latest` already moved by the time the gate kicked in. The gate defends the tag and the Release; nothing defends the registry. That's the asymmetry behind the mess I flagged — `latest` currently serves 1.9.0 while `v1.8.0` is still the newest tag.

If you want that tightened, the shape would be to push images under the version tag only, and move `latest` in a separate step after the smoke test passes. Worth its own issue under #899 rather than folding into #1003.

content.text:
I reproduced this locally — it's a `postgres:18` layout change, and `docker-compose.smoke.yml` is missing one line that the other compose files have.

Running the smoke file's db service standalone:

```
Error: in 18+, these Docker images are configured to store database data in a
       format which is compatible with "pg_ctlcluster" ...
       Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in:
         /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)
```

Postgres 18 moved the default `PGDATA` to a major-version subdirectory (`/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`) and made the container **refuse to start** when it finds a mount at the old `/var/lib/postgresql/data` path that nothing is using. Not a warning — exit 1, which is why compose reported `dependency failed to start`.

The reason dev and E2E work and smoke doesn't:

| file | tmpfs/volume | `PGDATA` set | works |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [docker-compose.dev.yml:21](docker-compose.dev.yml:21) | `dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` | yes | ✅ |
| [docker-compose.e2e.yml:23](docker-compose.e2e.yml:23) | `tmpfs: /var/lib/postgresql/data` | yes | ✅ |
| [docker-compose.smoke.yml:14](docker-compose.smoke.yml:14) | `tmpfs: /var/lib/postgresql/data` | **no** | ❌ |

Dev and E2E both pin `PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data`, which makes the mount *used* and satisfies the check. The smoke file was written from the same template but dropped that line, so `PGDATA` falls back to the 18 default, the mount becomes "unused", and the entrypoint bails.

**Fix — add the one line the other two have:**

```yaml
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: familytree
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: familytree
      POSTGRES_DB: familytree
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data
```

I verified the alternative too — moving the tmpfs to `/var/lib/postgresql` and dropping `PGDATA` entirely also starts cleanly (`accepting connections`), and it's what upstream actually recommends. But I'd go with the `PGDATA` line here: it makes smoke identical to the E2E config that's already proven in CI, and keeps all three files on one convention. Migrating all three to the upstream layout is worth doing eventually, but it invalidates existing dev volumes, so it deserves its own deliberate change rather than riding along on a release hotfix.

Want me to open that as a PR? It's a one-line change to `docker-compose.smoke.yml`, and it's the last thing standing between you and a green run — though note the smoke test is the *final* job, so it only gates the prerelease flag at that point, not the tag or the Release.
